title: Sha'ban: getting ready
hookLine: the Prophet ﷺ fasted much in Sha'ban (Bukhari), and some mark its middle night while others don't
tomorrow: Ramadan: the month of the Qur'an

cards: Nobody runs a marathon without training. Nobody plants a garden in the same hour they decide to have one; first you clear the weeds, turn the soil, wait for the right week.
Ramadan, a month of fasting from dawn to sunset, is a lot to step into cold.
And the month right before it, Sha'ban, has a reputation among Muslims as the month of getting ready. 'A'isha, the Prophet's ﷺ wife, noticed something about what he did in it.

teach.b: Bukhari records 'A'isha's words, roughly: I never saw the Messenger of God fast a whole month except Ramadan, and I never saw him fast more in any month than in Sha'ban. So it was his busiest month of voluntary fasting.
Why? A hadith in an-Nasa'i gives his own answer, through Usama ibn Zayd.
Sha'ban, he said, is a month people neglect, between Rajab and Ramadan, and it's a month when deeds are raised to God, and he loved for his deeds to be raised while he was fasting.
Between a sacred month and the holy month, people relax. He did the opposite. And yet there's a careful limit.
Another hadith in Bukhari says: don't fast a day or two right before Ramadan, unless it's a fast you already regularly keep. Getting ready doesn't mean rushing in early.
It means training through the month, then letting Ramadan begin on its own day.

teach.h: THE MIDDLE NIGHT, KEPT OR NOT.
teach.b: Then there's the middle night, the fifteenth of Sha'ban. Some Muslims, especially in South Asia, where it's called Shab-e-Barat, spend it in prayer, visit graves, and ask forgiveness.
For Twelver Shia Muslims, it is also the birth of the twelfth Imam, al-Mahdi.

Other Muslims don't mark the night specially, because some hadith scholars have judged the reports about it weak, and say the Prophet's practice was the steady fasting of the whole month, not one special night.
Both sides want the same thing: to arrive at Ramadan with the ground already turned.

how: Many Muslims increase voluntary fasting in Sha'ban to prepare for Ramadan; some communities spend the 15th night in prayer (Shab-e-Barat in South Asia, and for Twelver Shia also the Mahdi's birth), while others do not mark it.

games.q: Ramadan starts in two days. you want a head start, so you plan to fast tomorrow. what does the hadith say?
o: good idea: the more fasting, the better.
don't, unless it's a fast you already regularly keep.
fast two days, to be safe.
games.why: don't fast a day or two right before Ramadan unless it's your regular fast. train through the month, then let Ramadan begin on its own day.

practice: If you fast, choose one day this coming week to fast as practice, and picture how it will go: the early meal, the long afternoon, the evening.
If you don't, picture waking fifteen minutes early one morning, the way someone fasting rises for the pre-dawn meal. Notice what feels hard ahead of time.

wordCard.voice: Sha'ban. The month before Ramadan, when the Prophet fasted more than in any other month besides Ramadan: the month of getting ready. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Sha'ban, the eighth month of the Hijri year, just before Ramadan.
